??? question "What does the parser do after a syntax error so that it can keep checking the rest of the file?"

    Error recovery, usually by skipping ahead to a synchronization point such as `;` or `}`.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md). Specification: [10. Diagnostics](../../specification/diagnostics.md#105-recovery).

??? question "Which compiler stage turns the lowered program into instructions for a real processor?"

    The code generator. A linker then joins its output with the runtime library to make the executable.

    Introduced in [Overview](index.md).

??? question "What is the value a literal actually stands for, after `\n` has become a real line feed, called?"

    Its decoded value. The lexer must preserve it for each literal.

    Introduced in [2. The lexer](stage-2-lexer.md).

??? question "What do we call one small, automatic check with a definite pass or fail answer?"

    A test. It either passes or fails, with nothing in between.

    Introduced in [0. The workbench](stage-0-workbench.md).

??? question "What do we call instructions in the numeric form a processor can execute directly?"

    Machine code. A file of it that the operating system can start is an executable.

    Introduced in [Overview](index.md).

??? question "When nothing around it asks for another type, what type does a whole-number literal get, and a decimal one?"

    Their default types, `i32` for a whole number and `f32` for a decimal.

    Introduced in [Learn: 4. Variables and types](../../language-tour/04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [4. Types and values](../../specification/types-and-values.md#43-integers).

??? question "After a syntax error, at which tokens can the parser safely start again?"

    At synchronization points, such as `;`, `}` or the next `fn`.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md).

??? question "What is one symbol of text as a person would count it, such as a letter or `λ`, called?"

    A character. Some characters fit in one byte; others need several.

    Introduced in [1. Source text and error messages](stage-1-source-and-diagnostics.md).

??? question "Which well-known technique, named after Vaughan Pratt, parses expressions with many precedence levels?"

    Pratt parsing.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md).

??? question "What do we call something that used to work and has stopped working after a change, and how do you catch it?"

    A regression. You catch it by running every old test after every change.

    Introduced in [0. The workbench](stage-0-workbench.md).

??? question "In a syntax tree, what stands for one construct, such as one addition or one `if` statement?"

    A node. Literals and names are usually leaf nodes.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md).

??? question "In `struct Point { x: f32, y: f32 }`, what are `x` and `y` called, and how do you read one?"

    Fields. You read one through a value with a dot, as in `point.x`.

    Introduced in [Learn: 7. Declarations](../../language-tour/10-declarations.md). Specification: [8. Structs](../../specification/structs.md#84-field-access).

??? question "What kind of type is written as a plain name, such as `Point`, and must be matched to a struct declaration?"

    A named type. Name resolution finds the struct declaration it refers to.

    Introduced in [Learn: 4. Variables and types](../../language-tour/04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [4. Types and values](../../specification/types-and-values.md#411-type-equality).

??? question "What do we call a piece of code that produces a value, such as `2 + 3` or `square(4.0)`?"

    An expression. A statement, by contrast, does something and produces no value.

    Introduced in [Learn: 5. Expressions](../../language-tour/08-expressions.md). Specification: [5. Expressions](../../specification/expressions.md#51-expression-forms).

??? question "What is printed under a source line to show exactly which characters a diagnostic means?"

    A marker, such as a caret `^` under the characters in question.

    Introduced in [1. Source text and error messages](stage-1-source-and-diagnostics.md).

??? question "What do we call a value written directly in the source, such as `42` or `true`?"

    A literal. Integer, floating-point, boolean, character and string literals are the scalar forms.

    Introduced in [Learn: 5. Expressions](../../language-tour/08-expressions.md). Specification: [2. Lexical structure](../../specification/lexical-structure.md#25-literals).

??? question "Which values does the range `0..4` produce, and how do you include the end value?"

    The values 0, 1, 2 and 3; the end is excluded. Writing `0..=4` includes the end value.

    Introduced in [Learn: 5. Expressions](../../language-tour/08-expressions.md). Specification: [5. Expressions](../../specification/expressions.md#58-ranges).

??? question "Which statement changes the value of an existing variable, and what must be true of its target?"

    An assignment. Its target must be mutable storage, such as a variable declared with `mut`.

    Introduced in [Learn: 6. Statements](../../language-tour/09-statements.md). Specification: [6. Statements and control flow](../../specification/statements.md#64-assignment).

??? question "Which token has no spelling and marks where the input ends?"

    The end-of-file token. It gives later stages a clear place to stop.

    Introduced in [2. The lexer](stage-2-lexer.md).

??? question "Which compiler stage groups characters into tokens and skips whitespace and comments?"

    The lexer, also called the scanner.

    Introduced in [2. The lexer](stage-2-lexer.md). Specification: [2. Lexical structure](../../specification/lexical-structure.md).

??? question "What do braces with statements inside form, and what does each one create?"

    A block. Every block creates a new scope, so a variable declared inside it cannot be used after the closing brace.

    Introduced in [Learn: 6. Statements](../../language-tour/09-statements.md). Specification: [6. Statements and control flow](../../specification/statements.md#62-blocks).

??? question "What is one entry in the grammar, describing the shape of one construct, called?"

    A rule, also called a production.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md).

??? question "In a tree, what are the top node, a node directly below another, and a node with no children called?"

    The root, a child and a leaf. Literals and names are usually leaves.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md).

??? question "Which encoding stores plain English letters in one byte and other characters in two to four, and is used by Vortex strings?"

    UTF-8. A Vortex `String` stores UTF-8 text.

    Introduced in [1. Source text and error messages](stage-1-source-and-diagnostics.md). Specification: [4. Types and values](../../specification/types-and-values.md#46-characters-and-strings).

??? question "What is the hand-written parsing style in which each grammar rule becomes one piece that calls the pieces for the rules it contains?"

    Recursive descent.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md).

??? question "Why does `2 + 3 * 4` evaluate to 14 and not 20?"

    Because of precedence. `*` groups before `+`, so the expression means `2 + (3 * 4)`.

    Introduced in [Learn: 5. Expressions](../../language-tour/08-expressions.md). Specification: [5. Expressions](../../specification/expressions.md#52-precedence-and-associativity).

??? question "What tells the compiler what kind of value something is and what can be done with it?"

    Its type. Every Vortex expression has exactly one type, known before the program runs.

    Introduced in [Learn: 4. Variables and types](../../language-tour/04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [4. Types and values](../../specification/types-and-values.md).

??? question "What do we call the work of grouping characters into tokens?"

    Tokenizing, which the specification calls lexing.

    Introduced in [2. The lexer](stage-2-lexer.md). Specification: [12. Glossary](../../specification/glossary.md).

??? question "What kind of type is built into the language and named by a keyword, such as `i32` or `bool`?"

    A primitive type. v0.1 has `void`, `bool`, `char`, `i32`, `u32`, `usize`, `f32`, `f64` and `String`.

    Introduced in [Learn: 4. Variables and types](../../language-tour/04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [4. Types and values](../../specification/types-and-values.md#42-primitive-types).

??? question "Which kind of diagnostic reports that the tokens do not match the grammar, such as a missing `;`?"

    A syntax error. The parser reports it and then tries to recover.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md). Specification: [10. Diagnostics](../../specification/diagnostics.md#syntax-error).

??? question "Which part of the compiler holds the source text and turns offsets into lines and columns?"

    The source manager. It never interprets any syntax.

    Introduced in [1. Source text and error messages](stage-1-source-and-diagnostics.md).

??? question "What do we call the written rules for which token sequences form valid programs?"

    The grammar. For Vortex it is the formal grammar chapter of the specification.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md). Specification: [11. Formal grammar](../../specification/grammar.md).

??? question "What do we call a piece of code that does something, such as `return x;`, and does it produce a value in Vortex?"

    A statement. In Vortex a statement produces no value.

    Introduced in [Learn: 6. Statements](../../language-tour/09-statements.md). Specification: [6. Statements and control flow](../../specification/statements.md#61-statement-forms).

??? question "Which rule says which bytes stand for which characters?"

    An encoding. UTF-8 is the most common one.

    Introduced in [1. Source text and error messages](stage-1-source-and-diagnostics.md).

??? question "What do we call a program that reads source code, checks it, and writes out code a machine can run?"

    A compiler. It also rejects programs that break the rules and explains the problem.

    Introduced in [Overview](index.md).

??? question "Inside a string or character literal, what do we call `\n` or `\t`?"

    An escape sequence, a backslash and a character that stand for something hard to type. v0.1 supports `\n`, `\t`, `\\`, `\"` and `\'`.

    Introduced in [Learn: 2. Basic source rules](../../language-tour/02-basic-source-rules.md). Specification: [2. Lexical structure](../../specification/lexical-structure.md#character-and-string-literals).

??? question "What do we call the list of an array's sizes, one per dimension?"

    Its shape. For `[f32; 2, 3]` the shape is `[2, 3]`, and it is part of the type.

    Introduced in [Learn: 4. Variables and types](../../language-tour/04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../../specification/arrays.md#75-rank-and-shape).

??? question "Which kind of diagnostic says that some characters cannot form any valid token?"

    A lexical error, for example an unterminated string or an unsupported escape.

    Introduced in [2. The lexer](stage-2-lexer.md). Specification: [10. Diagnostics](../../specification/diagnostics.md#lexical-error).

??? question "What do we call a position in a source file counted from its start?"

    An offset. It is easy for a program to store, but people need line and column instead.

    Introduced in [1. Source text and error messages](stage-1-source-and-diagnostics.md).

??? question "What are spaces, tabs and line breaks called, and what do they do in Vortex?"

    Whitespace. It separates tokens and means nothing else; a line break does not end a statement.

    Introduced in [2. The lexer](stage-2-lexer.md). Specification: [2. Lexical structure](../../specification/lexical-structure.md#21-whitespace-and-line-boundaries).

??? question "What is the file of Vortex text handed to the compiler called?"

    The source file, a sequence of source characters provided to the compiler.

    Introduced in [1. Source text and error messages](stage-1-source-and-diagnostics.md). Specification: [1. Conformance and terminology](../../specification/conformance.md#12-programs).

??? question "What do we call a burst of false errors caused by one real mistake?"

    A cascade. It happens when the parser gets confused about where it is.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md).

??? question "What is the process that turns the compiler's own source code into the `vortex` program called?"

    The build. The build system is the tool that knows the recipe.

    Introduced in [0. The workbench](stage-0-workbench.md).

??? question "What do we call the exact characters a token was made from, and what do many books call it?"

    Its spelling, also called the lexeme.

    Introduced in [2. The lexer](stage-2-lexer.md).

??? question "Why does the lexer read `<=` as one token rather than `<` followed by `=`?"

    Because of the longest-match rule, also called maximal munch. When several tokens could start at the same place, the lexer takes the longest valid one.

    Introduced in [2. The lexer](stage-2-lexer.md). Specification: [2. Lexical structure](../../specification/lexical-structure.md#26-operators-and-punctuation).

??? question "How does a diagnostic describe a position so that a person can find it?"

    By line and column, which row of the file and how far along that row.

    Introduced in [1. Source text and error messages](stage-1-source-and-diagnostics.md).

??? question "What sorts diagnostics into kinds such as lexical error or type error, and how many kinds does the specification list?"

    The category. The specification lists eight.

    Introduced in [1. Source text and error messages](stage-1-source-and-diagnostics.md). Specification: [10. Diagnostics](../../specification/diagnostics.md#102-categories).

??? question "What do we call a test program written on purpose to break exactly one rule?"

    An invalid program. The compiler must reject it.

    Introduced in [0. The workbench](stage-0-workbench.md).

??? question "In the call `add(3, 4)`, what are `3` and `4` called?"

    Arguments. Each one supplies the value for one parameter, and their number and types must match the parameter list.

    Introduced in [Learn: 7. Declarations](../../language-tour/10-declarations.md). Specification: [5. Expressions](../../specification/expressions.md#calls).

??? question "What does the specification call checking the grammatical structure of a token stream and building the AST?"

    Parsing, the job of the parser.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md). Specification: [12. Glossary](../../specification/glossary.md).

??? question "Which program finds all the test cases, runs the compiler on each, and reports pass or fail?"

    The test runner. It compares what happened with each test's expected output.

    Introduced in [0. The workbench](stage-0-workbench.md).

??? question "What is text for human readers that the compiler skips called, and how is it written in v0.1?"

    A comment. It starts with `//` and runs to the end of the line; block comments are not part of v0.1.

    Introduced in [Learn: 2. Basic source rules](../../language-tour/02-basic-source-rules.md). Specification: [2. Lexical structure](../../specification/lexical-structure.md#22-comments).

??? question "What is the text of a program as a person wrote it called?"

    Source code. It is what the compiler reads.

    Introduced in [Overview](index.md).

??? question "Does `a - b - c` mean `(a - b) - c` or `a - (b - c)`, and which rule decides?"

    Associativity decides. Most Vortex binary operators are left-associative, so it means `(a - b) - c`.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md). Specification: [5. Expressions](../../specification/expressions.md#52-precedence-and-associativity).

??? question "Which part of the compiler reads the tokens, checks them against the grammar and builds a syntax tree?"

    The parser. It reports a syntax error when the tokens do not fit the grammar.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md). Specification: [11. Formal grammar](../../specification/grammar.md).

??? question "What does the lexer hand to the parser?"

    The token stream, every token of the file in order, ending with an end-of-file token.

    Introduced in [2. The lexer](stage-2-lexer.md).

??? question "What do we call a compiler whose driver runs and exits properly but translates nothing yet?"

    An empty compiler. Milestone 0 is done when it builds reliably and the test runner reports a pass and a fail.

    Introduced in [0. The workbench](stage-0-workbench.md).

??? question "Which tree keeps only the meaningful parts of a program and drops punctuation whose job the tree's shape already shows?"

    The abstract syntax tree (AST), which the guide simply calls the syntax tree.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md). Specification: [12. Glossary](../../specification/glossary.md).

??? question "What do we call a build that starts from nothing, with no leftover files or machine-specific settings?"

    A clean configuration, with no files from an earlier build and no settings that exist only on one person's machine.

    Introduced in [0. The workbench](stage-0-workbench.md).

??? question "What do we call a program the specification says the compiler must accept?"

    A valid program. Its opposite, an invalid program, must be rejected.

    Introduced in [0. The workbench](stage-0-workbench.md).

??? question "What does every token, tree node and error message carry to say exactly which stretch of source it came from?"

    A source span, a start position and a length.

    Introduced in [1. Source text and error messages](stage-1-source-and-diagnostics.md). Specification: [1. Conformance and terminology](../../specification/conformance.md#17-source-locations).

??? question "Which extra line on a diagnostic can point at a second, related place, such as an earlier declaration?"

    A note. It helps explain why the primary span is wrong.

    Introduced in [1. Source text and error messages](stage-1-source-and-diagnostics.md).

??? question "What is the 8-bit unit that files and memory are stored in called?"

    A byte. It holds one of 256 values, and one character may need several bytes.

    Introduced in [1. Source text and error messages](stage-1-source-and-diagnostics.md).

??? question "Which written record does a test compare against to decide whether it passed?"

    The expected output, such as the program's printed text or the error's kind and location.

    Introduced in [0. The workbench](stage-0-workbench.md).

??? question "For a compiler, what is the material for one test usually made of, and what is it called?"

    A test case, one Vortex source file together with a description of what should happen to it.

    Introduced in [0. The workbench](stage-0-workbench.md).

??? question "Which tool knows the recipe for building the compiler?"

    The build system. It turns the compiler's source code into the `vortex` program.

    Introduced in [0. The workbench](stage-0-workbench.md).

??? question "Which span of a diagnostic is the one it is about, where the marker points?"

    The primary span. Notes may point at other, related spans.

    Introduced in [1. Source text and error messages](stage-1-source-and-diagnostics.md).

??? question "What number does a program hand back when it finishes, and which value means success?"

    Its exit status. By convention zero means success and anything else means failure.

    Introduced in [0. The workbench](stage-0-workbench.md).

??? question "What do we call a message from the compiler about a problem in the source?"

    A diagnostic. In v0.1 every diagnostic is an error and carries a source location.

    Introduced in [1. Source text and error messages](stage-1-source-and-diagnostics.md). Specification: [10. Diagnostics](../../specification/diagnostics.md#101-required-diagnostic-data).

??? question "What is `matrix[row, column]` an example of, and what must its indices be?"

    Indexing. There must be one integer index for each dimension of the array.

    Introduced in [Learn: 5. Expressions](../../language-tour/08-expressions.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../../specification/arrays.md#76-indexing).

??? question "What do we call a word such as `let`, `fn` or `while` that the language reserves and that cannot be used as a name?"

    A keyword. Matching is case-sensitive, so `String` is a keyword but `string` is an identifier.

    Introduced in [2. The lexer](stage-2-lexer.md). Specification: [2. Lexical structure](../../specification/lexical-structure.md#24-keywords).

??? question "Which property of a token says whether it is a keyword, an identifier, an integer literal or an operator?"

    Its token kind. With the spelling and the source span, it describes the token.

    Introduced in [2. The lexer](stage-2-lexer.md).

??? question "What is one size in an array type such as `[f32; 4, 8]` called, and when must it be known?"

    A dimension. Each one must evaluate at compile time to an integer that fits `usize`.

    Introduced in [Learn: 4. Variables and types](../../language-tour/04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../../specification/arrays.md#72-dimension-rules).

??? question "What do we call a place in the program that introduces a name, such as `let width = 128;`?"

    A declaration. Top-level declarations are functions and structs; locals are declared by statements inside blocks.

    Introduced in [Learn: 7. Declarations](../../language-tour/10-declarations.md). Specification: [3. Programs and declarations](../../specification/declarations.md#31-program-structure).

??? question "Which kind of tree has a node for every grammar rule the parser used, including punctuation?"

    A parse tree, also called a concrete syntax tree.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md).

??? question "What do we call one unit of the language, such as a keyword, a name, a number or a symbol?"

    A token. Each token has a kind, a spelling and a source span.

    Introduced in [2. The lexer](stage-2-lexer.md). Specification: [2. Lexical structure](../../specification/lexical-structure.md#28-token-source-data).

??? question "What happens when a running Vortex program divides an integer by zero?"

    A runtime error. The program stops and reports what went wrong.

    Introduced in [Learn: 8. Runtime and numerical rules](../../language-tour/06-runtime-and-numerical-rules.md). Specification: [10. Diagnostics](../../specification/diagnostics.md#runtime-error).

??? question "What is the program a person runs to use the compiler, which runs the stages in order and reports the outcome?"

    The driver. For Vortex it is the `vortex` command.

    Introduced in [0. The workbench](stage-0-workbench.md).

??? question "What is the parser doing when it peeks at the next token without using it up, to decide which rule applies?"

    Using lookahead. It lets the parser choose a rule before committing to it.

    Introduced in [3. The parser and the syntax tree](stage-3-parser-and-tree.md).
